HMB.about: HMB is a metabolite of leucine: preserves muscle in cancer patients (review 2022) and increases walking speed in sarcopenia with exercise (MA 2024).
HMB.caution: In reviews, safety was comparable to placebo; the effects are concentrated in clinical groups—do not exaggerate expectations in healthy people.
HMB.course: Weeks to months, along with a training program or nutritional support.
HMB.dosage: Ca-HMB 3 g/day (80% of studies in SR 2022).
HMB.food_sources: HMB - metabolite, no food source; substrate leucine - in meat, fish, eggs, dairy products.
HMB.guidelines: JCSM 2022 (CP 15 papers, cancer): muscle mass 4/4, function 2/2, hospitalizations 3/3; MA 2024 (5 RCT): walking speed SMD 0.48; umbrella 2021: low-moderate confidence.
HMB.how_to_choose: Ca-HMB form, ~3 g/day (according to research schemes); target groups - patients and elderly people with stress; There is no data for sports outside the context of these reviews.
mechs: Slows muscle protein breakdown and supports protein synthesis
preservation of muscle mass and function in patients with cancer (4/4)
HMB and clinical outcomes in risk groups
reduction in hospitalizations, trend towards better survival
HMB.myths: “HMB is an anabolic for everyone” - data mainly in patients and the elderly. “Works on its own” - effects are often combined. “Added and the muscles grow” - no effect was found on grip strength and weight in MA 2024.
HMB.name: HMB
HMB.onset: Course from weeks to months: effects on weight and function are described when taking ~3 g/day; in MA 2024, walking speed increased as part of training.
HMB.title: HMB
HMB.who_needs: Patients with cancer under therapy - maintenance of muscle mass (Ca-HMB ~3 g/day in 80% of studies); elderly with sarcopenia - as part of exercise programs; otherwise data is limited.
